abstract: Foxtail millet is rich in unsaturated lipids and is susceptible to oxidative deterioration during storage. In this study, foxtail millet flour was stored at 50 °C and 60% relative humidity for 0-8 weeks to trace lipid remodeling and volatile formation. Unsaturated fatty acids declined markedly, with linoleic acid decreasing from 547.06 ± 1.11 to 383.73 ± 3.13 mg/g. Lipidomics identified 72 lipid species, with TGs as the predominant class, and showed depletion of structural lipids represented by PC 18:2_18:2 and MGDG 18:2_18:2, together with accumulation of oxidized lipids such as FA 18:2;O. Volatilomics detected 51 volatiles, among which 1-dodecanol, 1-undecanol, and nonanal were storage-related markers. These results suggest that storage-induced lipid deterioration involved the disruption of structural lipids, hydrolysis of triacylglycerols, and oxidation of unsaturated acyl chains, ultimately promoting the formation of aldehydes and alcohols associated with flavor deterioration.
